- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 73.08 or 72.86), then undercorrects, leading to persistent overprediction.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting a mean-reversion bias or lag in capturing tail risks.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, missing volatility spikes and sudden reversals.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the 30-day forecast, particularly when history shows sustained upward momentum.
- When history includes a recent peak, model often fails to adjust downward quickly, leading to overcorrection lag.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “climb too fast” and then “drop too late,” suggesting poor handling of momentum decay.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., 2024-09-02), model overreacts to minor fluctuations, producing erratic forecasts that diverge from true mean.
